operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are plain upper-case ASCII, no spaces/mixed case; quoting still required by spec.
Tiny DB (7/6/7 rows); read_schema sampling is a no-op, original_values are complete.
BIGINT declared type: not in the number-family list literally? 'int' substring matches -> Number fuzzer, is_int=True, scale=0, precision=0 (no args).
FLOAT -> Number fuzzer, is_int=False, scale=0, precision=0 (no args); range [-1,1] then perturbed by +-0.01/0.02.
VARCHAR(64) -> String fuzzer with length=64 (args[0]); CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() only.
custid storage integer, balance storage real: consistent with declared types, no contradiction.
FKs SAVINGS.custid->ACCOUNTS.custid and CHECKING.custid->ACCOUNTS.custid both exist and parent is unique PK; no dangling FKs.
All three tables have single-column PK custid; SAVINGS/CHECKING PK is also the FK column (child PK = FK).
No composite keys, no self-references, no views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs.
NOT NULL on every column; no CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE beyond PK.
name samples include apostrophe (O'mahony) and mixed case; String fuzzer will not reproduce apostrophes (CHARSET lacks ').
balance samples include 999999999.0 (near 1e9) far outside Number's [-1,1] range; original values only enter via 5 rng.choices elements.
operator_ts_expectations: custid (BIGINT, PK, Number is_int): fresh draws uniform in [-1,1] then int-perturbed (+-1/+-2) -> mostly small ints like -3..3; PK dedup keeps first occurrence, so ACCOUNTS gets ~7 distinct small ints.

SAVINGS/CHECKING custid: FK fill draws from ACCOUNTS.custid final values with replacement -> subset of ACCOUNTS keys, PK dedup on child reduces to distinct subset; child row count <= parent distinct count.
balance (FLOAT, Number): fresh draws in [-1,1] perturbed by +-0.01/0.02 -> values like -1.02..1.02; original 200000/999999999 never sampled unless rng
name (VARCHAR(64), String): fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() length 0..64, plus 50% contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop char); original names Brown/Wang/O'mahony only via element path.
p=0.2 default, whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3 -> in ~30% of instances every column always returns an element (original or pool value), so balance/name become near-original.

max_l0 cap: single-column PK -> inf (custid always fresh); non-PK columns get max_l0 = rng.random()*30, so after ~0-30 fresh draws they reuse a previous fresh value -> low distinct counts on balance/name.

Table sizes: rand_lin path gives int(30*u + u2*200) ~ 30..230 rows per table; level path gives level0=1+30u, next x4 capped 2500 -> SAVINGS/CHECKING can be 4x ACCOUNTS, but FK+PK dedup caps them at ACCOUNTS distinct count.
Likely FN driver: balance values clustered in [-1,1] make SUM/AVG/MAX comparisons on balance implausible vs gold (gold uses 200000/999999999); queries filtering balance>1000 return empty.

Likely FP driver: custid small ints (-3..3) collide with literal pool ints from train SQL (e.g. custid=1,2,3) so equality/join predicates match spuriously; also name random strings rarely equal gold names -> name predicates mostly empty (FN).
FK consistency holds (child custid subset of parent), so join queries ACCOUNTS-join-SAVINGS return rows; but child PK=FK means at most one row per custid, matching original cardinality.
No NOT NULL/CHECK violations expected: all columns NOT NULL but Number/String fuzzers never emit None (Base drops None, p=1 if empty), so inserts succeed; rows_failed ~0.
